<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. X.|ACCORDING TO S. MARKE.|113}}</noinclude>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text={{sc|The third}} part of this Gospel, Christes cōming into Iewrie toward his Passion.}}{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. X.}}}}}}

{{c|''He answereth the tempting Pharisees (and againe his disciples afterward) that the case of a man with his wife shalbe (as in the first institution) vtterly indissoluble. 13 He blesseth children. 17 He sheweth what is to be done to get life euerlasting. 21 What also for a rich man, to be perfect: 28 as also what passing reward they shal haue that doe so in time of persecution. 32 He reuealeth more to his Disciples touching his Passion: 35 bidding the two ambitious suiters to thinke rather of suffering with him: 41 and teaching vs in the rest of his Disciples, not to be greeued at our Ecclesiastical Superiours, considering they are (as he was him self) to toile for our saluation. 46 Then going out of Iericho, he giueth sight to a blinde man.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=10|verse=1}}}}{{sc|Nd}} rising vp thence, he commeth into the coastes of Ievvrie beyond Iordan: and the multitudes assemble againe vnto him. and as he vvas accustomed, againe he taught them.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 19, 1.''}} {{verse|chapter=10|verse=2}}† And the Pharisees comming neere, asked him, Is it lavvful for a man to dimisse his vvife? tempting him. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=3}}† But he ansvvering, said to them, VVhat did Moyses commaund you? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=4}}† Who said, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Deut. 24, 1.''}}* Moyses {{sup|‖}} permitted to vvrite a bil of diuorce, and to dimisse her. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=5}}† To vvhom {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering, said, For the hardnes of your hart he vvrote you this precept. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=6}}† but from the beginning of the creation {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 1, 27.''}}* God made them male and femal. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=7}}† For this cause, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 2, 24.''}}* man shal leaue his father and mother: and shal cleaue to his vvife, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=8}}† and they tvvo shal be in one flesh. therfore novv they are not tvvo, but one flesh. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=9}}† That therfore vvhich God hath ioyned together, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The obligation betwixt man and wife is so great, that during life it can not be broken.}}∷ let not man separate. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=10}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 19, 9. Mt. 5, 32. Lu. 16, 18. 1. Cor. 7, 11.''}}* in the house againe his Disciples asked him of the same thing. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=11}}† And he saith to them, Whosoeuer dimisseth his vvife {{sup|‖}} and marrieth an other: committeth aduoutrie vpon her. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=12}}† And if the vvife dimisse her husband, and mary an other, she committeth aduoutrie.

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=13}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 19, 13. Lu. 18, 15.''}}* they offered to him yong children, that he might touche them. And the Disciples threatened those that offered them. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=14}}† Whom vvhen {{sc|Iesvs}} savv, he tooke it il, and said to them, Suffer the litle children to come vnto me, and prohibit them not. for the kingdom of God is for such. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=15}}† Amen I say to you: Whosoeuer receiueth not the kingdom of God as a litle childe, shal not enter into it. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=16}}† And embracing them, and imposing hands vpon them, he {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Our Sauiour gaue the children his blessing, imposing his hands vpon them.}}∷ blessed them.

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=17}}† And vvhen he vvas gone forth in the vvay, a certaine man running forth and kneeling before him asked him,<noinclude>{{rh||P|Good}}</noinclude>
